content.comment_body: Hello, I need to connect two units of [product_name] [version_no] controllers to two different WiFi routers. Scenario details: Location A: [product_name] [version_no] 1 connected to WiFi Router 1 via Ethernet cable Location B: [product_name] [version_no] 2 connected to WiFi Router 2 via Ethernet cable When Input 1 (I1) of [product_name] [version_no] 1 is active, I want to trigger Output 1 (Q1) of [product_name] [version_no] 2, and vice versa. I can use WiFi or SMS (using the [product_name] Communication Module option). The SMS option is straightforward, but I would like to know if it's possible to do this via WiFi routers (2 units) instead of SMS. Any advice is appreciated.

This solution works well if the distance is not excessive and stable data transmission is assured. Also, both [product_name] controllers need to be on the same subnet. For longer distances, there are purpose-built WiFi routers you can consider.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion focuses on connecting two [product_name] controllers at separate locations via WiFi routers. The main concern is reliably linking the controllers over WiFi when they are not within the same subnet. Users compare the feasibility and limits of using WiFi routers versus [product_name] Communication Modules, highlighting configuration complexity and the need for dependable communication.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a simple and dependable method for two-way control between [product_name] controllers using WiFi routers, preferring not to use [product_name] Communication Modules or require both devices to be on the same subnet. Reliable, straightforward communication over WiFi is the goal.
